decision: Publish manually reviewed collection notes and two unchanged original reference PDFs. Preserve accepted prose and all existing imagery. No later screenshots or geological maps are substituted for original NZLRI or LADEDA outputs.

notes.title: Finding the paper records at Hocken
notes.text: Hocken’s Maps and plans guide explains how to find maps, charts, plans and aerial photographs. Published mapping is searched through Library Search | Ketu; archival maps and plans through Hākena. This is a present-day route into the records described here.
notes.limitations: The guide is not a complete inventory. A catalogue entry does not establish that an item has been digitised.

notes.title: From Crown film negatives to Retrolens
notes.text: LINZ identifies its aerial-photo footprint layer as the comprehensive catalogue of the Crown Aerial Film Library. Retrolens provides an interactive route to many surveys, with downloads at lower resolution than the original scans. Survey, run and frame identifiers remain essential when comparing images.
notes.limitations: A photograph is not automatically an orthorectified map. Capture dates, frame identity and positional limitations must be checked for each use.

notes.title: Hector’s geological map of Otago
notes.text: Hocken preserves a large geological map attributed to James Hector and dated 1864, at approximately four miles to one inch. Simon Nathan’s curatorial account cautions that it may be a later copy using a later topographic base. It differs from the eight-mile-to-the-inch map listed for the 1865 Dunedin exhibition.
notes.limitations: The date on the map does not resolve the date of this surviving object. It is geological mapping, not a LUC survey or NZLRI worksheet.

notes.title: Following the inventory into Our Environment
notes.text: Manaaki Whenua’s Our Environment documentation connects online LRI and LUC layers to regional-scale mapping. Its provenance page distinguishes original 1:63,360 boundaries from later 1:50,000 mapping. The December 2021 LUC update reconciled classification units and descriptions without changing the underlying geometry.
notes.limitations: The current service is a later access layer. Its maps must not be presented as original 1967 survey sheets, first-edition NZLRI worksheets or LADEDA outputs.

notes.title: The Historic Geological Map Archive
notes.text: GNS describes an archive of more than 9,000 geological maps and field sheets, including field mapping, draft compilations and published sheets. Its pre-2012 holdings were scanned at high resolution and georeferenced during the 2010s. The collection retains the earlier interpretation behind later geological GIS.
notes.limitations: An archive scan is not evidence of the original map’s digital production. Identify the item’s author, date, scale and publication state before using it as an illustration.

notes.title: University access to cartographic and GIS resources
notes.text: Igor Drecki’s 2019 GeoDataHub abstract describes the University of Auckland Library bringing digitised maps, charts, aerial photography and spatial datasets into one repository, alongside its physical Map Room collection. It records catalogue discovery through GeoNetwork and different access routes for public and university users.
notes.limitations: This later example illustrates university data access; it does not establish what was available in a particular 1980s GIS class.

notes.title: Geographx and Unfolding the Map
notes.text: The National Library’s October 2015 account identifies Roger Smith of Geographx as curator of Unfolding the Map. The exhibition drew on Turnbull and Archives New Zealand collections and connected earlier cartography with GPS, interactive mapping and digital terrain. Its Tasman River illustration is credited to Smith.
notes.limitations: The exhibition is a documented example of cartographic presentation. Its modern terrain image is not an illustration of an early NZLRI or LADEDA system.

notes.title: An environmental service built from open components
notes.text: Our Environment’s institutional account identifies an open-source platform including PostgreSQL/PostGIS, MapServer, GDAL, GEOS and OpenLayers. These components sit behind a public mapping and reporting service, providing a concrete example of open databases, processing libraries and web mapping working together.

links.label: Our Environment: service history and platform

notes.limitations: The platform description records the service documented by the institution. It does not date the adoption of each individual component.

notes.title: From LRIS downloads to a public land atlas
notes.text: Manaaki Whenua dates the first Our Environment release to 2011. It provides maps and reports for users who do not need desktop GIS, while directing users to the LRIS Portal for downloadable data and to separate WMS and WMTS services. These are distinct routes into related science datasets.

links.label: Our Environment: history and access routes

notes.limitations: The 2011 date belongs to Our Environment, not the separate LRIS Portal launch in 2010.

notes.title: Reading the metadata before reuse
notes.text: Our Environment’s provenance statement describes its LRI polygons as regional-scale information and explains differences in mapping scale and attribute uncertainty. Its guidance makes a useful companion to the point here: access to a spatial layer does not establish its fitness for a particular analysis.
notes.limitations: Current metadata may describe revised classifications and layers. Consult edition and update information before comparing it with historical outputs.

The file metadata gives a creation date in April 2026; this is not treated as a printed publication date. Some catalogue entries describe undigitised holdings.

unresolved.decision: The published viewer uses Zoomify tiles. No standalone full-resolution original downloaded. Exact map date remains qualified by Simon Nathan’s account. Linked the original institutional viewer and curatorial explanation; no image derivative published.
Collection identity and scope verified, but no item-specific original selected for a precise accepted paragraph in this release. Catalogue linked; no generic map substituted.
Still unresolved. Current LRIS/Our Environment access does not establish the identity of a complete first-edition original worksheet.
